name: The Meatmen
label: Touch and Go
lede: Robert Vermeulen taught third and fifth grade in Williamston, Michigan, and ran a punk zine off the school copier at 3 a.m. As Tesco Vee he fronted the Meatmen, the dirtiest band in hardcore, and by 1983 had two Minor Threat guitarists playing behind him.

eras.title: A teacher with a copy machine
eras.text: Robert Vermeulen taught third and fifth grade in Williamston, Michigan. At night he was Tesco Vee, co-editor of the Lansing punk zine Touch and Go, which grew into the label behind Big Black and Butthole Surfers, and singer in a band built to offend everyone.

years.src: Vice: The Meatmen Are Back · Wikipedia: Tesco Vee · Westword: Tesco Vee on punk in Michigan
years.h: Tesco Vee runs a punk zine off the school photocopier at 3 a.m.
years.p: Vee, a grade-school teacher, and high school classmate Dave Stimson start Touch and Go in East Lansing.
years.xp:
"I used to sneak in at 3 AM and make photocopies for the zine," Vee told Vice.

The zine ran 22 issues.

years.h: The early hits get written in an attic in East Lansing
years.p: Vee gathers high school friends there in 1979. Punk's do-it-yourself idea, he told Vice, made him realize he could get onstage too.
years.xp: Vee's own account of that first practice: he and his friends "drank a bunch of swill and came up with all the early hits."

years.h: A frying-pan bartender watches the Meatmen's first show
years.p: The Meatmen debut at the Coronation Tavern in Windsor, Ontario. Vee remembers the bartender hitting customers with a frying pan.

years.h: Touch and Go's first record has Meatmen Stomp on it
years.p: Touch and Go becomes a label, with [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] bassist [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] helping. The Process of Elimination 7" sampler puts the Meatmen next to [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]].

years.h: Fear plays Saturday Night Live, and Vee is in the pit
years.p: John Belushi brings a hardcore crowd to NBC for [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]]'s Halloween 1981 set. Vee dances alongside Detroit's [[John Brannon|a3418f6c-a8b1-4565-9836-b389b405510a]] and kids from D.C.

eras.title: A riot on Cass Avenue, then a one-way trip to D.C.
eras.text: The Meatmen titled their records to get banned and played the same bills as Minor Threat and Negative Approach. By 1983 Vee had lost his teaching job, handed Touch and Go to Corey Rusk and headed for Washington.

years.h: Blüd Sausage arrives with seven songs and titles built to offend
years.p: Touch and Go releases the band's first EP. It becomes the studio side of their 1983 album.
years.xp: Trouser Press lists a second 1982 EP, Crippled Children Suck, also on Touch and Go; Wikipedia dates it 1983. Song titles like Camel Jockeys Suck and One Down Three to Go were written to offend and did.

years.h: A Cass Avenue bill with Minor Threat ends in a parking-lot riot
years.p: Metro Times puts the Meatmen on the bill with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] at Detroit's Freezer Theater. Broken windows and arrests follow, and the venue closes for good.

years.h: Vee loses his teaching job and moves to D.C.
years.p: He told Razorcake he lost the job around 1982, as everyone left Michigan for the Texas oil boom. A visit to a D.C. show with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]] had already hooked him.
years.xp: Vee's description of the D.C. scene that won him over: "Ian and Henry, the big boys in that little scene." Ian is [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]; Henry is [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]].

years.src: Wikipedia: We're the Meatmen...and You Suck!!
years.h: We're the Meatmen...and You Suck!! pairs the EP with a live set
years.p: The live half, recorded in New York City, includes Meatmen Stomp and Mister Tapeworm. Sixteen tracks in all.
years.xp: The line-up was Tesco Vee with Rich and Greg Ramsey on guitars, Mike Achtenburg on bass and drummers credited as Mr. X and Berl Johnson. Some sources call it a compilation, others a live album; many fans count it as the debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · Chunklet
years.h: Touch and Go goes to Corey and Lisa Rusk when Vee leaves Michigan
years.p: The Rusks later move the label to Chicago. Vee told Chunklet he'd never have predicted how big it got.
years.xp: Under the Rusks the label signed [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]], [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]], [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] and [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]], on handshake deals that split profits 50–50 with the bands.

eras.title: Minor Threat in evening gowns
eras.text: In D.C. the Meatmen became a supergroup of sorts: two Minor Threat guitarists and Negative Approach's bassist behind a singer in costume. The records moved to Homestead and Caroline, and the joke got bigger and louder.

years.cap: Minor Threat at the Wilson Center, Washington, D.C., April 4, 1981: Lyle Preslar and Brian Baker, two years before they joined the Meatmen
years.h: Two Minor Threat guitarists sign on as Vee's D.C. Meatmen
years.p: After [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] ends, [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]] and [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] become Tesco Vee's new backing band.

years.h: Negative Approach's Graham McCulloch joins on bass
years.p: The Detroit bassist ties Vee's old Michigan scene to his new D.C. band. [[Graham McCulloch|a9cb94ec-b297-44d5-9ea1-dbefe4b26c33]] stays until 1988.
years.xp:
The same year Trouser Press credits Vee with a solo EP, Dutch Hercules, made with Preslar and Baker.

A full set from Philadelphia on June 16, 1984, with the D.C. line-up, is on YouTube.

yt: Live at City Gardens, Trenton, September 8, 1985
years.h: Ian MacKaye produces War of the Superbikes
years.p: The first D.C. Meatmen album, on Homestead, has Preslar and Baker on guitars and their old Minor Threat singer at the board.

years.src: Vice: The Meatmen Are Back · Trouser Press: Meatmen
years.h: Brian Baker leaves, tired of the ballerina costumes
years.p: According to Vee, Baker was sick of wearing ballerina costumes and evening gowns onstage. His next band is [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]].
years.xp: James Cooper took over Baker's guitar spot for the next album, according to Trouser Press.

years.big: "For a lot of people, that's their favorite Meatmen record."
yt: Live at the 9:30 Club, Washington, D.C., January 8, 1986
years.h: Rock 'n' Roll Juggernaut goofs on heavy metal for Caroline
years.p: Vee on his 1986 album for Caroline Records, speaking to Razorcake years later.
years.xp:
"We're goofing on metal in 1986 and, for a lot of people, that's their favorite Meatmen record. So go figure."

A January 1986 set at the 9:30 Club in D.C. is on YouTube.

years.h: The D.C. Meatmen call it quits on a farewell tour
years.p: Caroline releases the live We're the Meatmen...and You Still Suck!!! in 1989.

eras.title: Retired, again
eras.text: Vee couldn't stay retired. A third Meatmen line-up made three more records in the mid-nineties before he announced, again, that he was done.

years.h: Vee brings the Meatmen back on his own Meatking label
years.p: A new line-up starts recording for Meatking. Toilet Slave follows in 1994.

years.h: The nineties Meatmen answer with Pope on a Rope
years.p: The mid-nineties line-up's second album. War of the Superbikes II follows in 1996.

years.h: Vee quits performing and writes a song called Dinosaur
years.p: He stops in 1996, the same year he writes Dinosaur, about playing punk since 1979.

years.h: Vee goes home to Michigan
years.p: He leaves the Washington, D.C. area after seventeen years.

eras.title: Negative Approach brings him back
eras.text: A reissue, a Detroit show backed by Negative Approach and a push from his son put Vee back onstage in his fifties, with a band half his age.

years.h: Touch and Go reissues Blight, Vee's old noise band
years.p: Blight, Vee's early-eighties side project with ex-members of Lansing's [[The Fix|75b206a3-acca-4a37-8e4d-c29fbb0cba22]], gets a Touch and Go reissue.

years.cap: Tesco Vee in a flag-print jacket, May 15, 2008
years.src: Razorcake: Interview with Tesco Vee · Vice: The Meatmen Are Back
years.h: Negative Approach backs Vee for thirty minutes in Detroit
years.p: [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] plays behind Vee for the set. He credits the show, and his son's encouragement, with bringing the Meatmen back.
years.xp:
"I got up on stage and I was like, 'Man I can do this shit!'" Vee told Razorcake.

By late 2008 he had a new line-up of musicians in their twenties, some from the band Chapstik, and plans for a covers album. His son worked as the band's road manager for a couple of years.

A BlankTV interview with Vee from April 2011 is on YouTube.

years.cap: Tesco Vee with the reunited Meatmen, holding a sign overhead, March 15, 2008
years.h: The Meatmen cover Black Randy, Thin Lizzy and ABBA
years.p: The title Cover the Earth comes from the Sherwin-Williams paint slogan. Jimmy Dean gets a cover too.

years.cap: Tesco Vee with the Meatmen, Chicago, April 29, 2011
years.src: Westword: Tesco Vee on punk in Michigan · Wikipedia: Tesco Vee
years.h: Bazillion Points puts every issue of the zine in one book
years.p: Touch and Go: The Complete Hardcore Punk Zine '79–'83 collects everything Vee and Stimson made. Westword reported 8,000 copies sold.
years.xp: The book runs to more than 500 pages.

years.h: Savage Sagas, the first new Meatmen songs in twenty years
years.p: Released on Self Destructo Records. Vee told Vice a legacy punk band has to really bring it every night.
years.xp: "My son really inspired me to re-light the fuse," Vee told Vice.

years.h: Vee's own toys fill a new shop in Lansing
years.p: The store carries puppets, coloring books, figurines, character dolls and model kits from the 1940s to the 1980s.
